author: Michael Caldwell
title: Caldwell: Transcending the divide | Commentary | timesargus.com
text:
My friend David’s Belgian beauties skid maple and beech logs to his landing. He brakes Barbara and Bette with his soothing voice, unhitches them, unharnesses them, and puts them to grazing. We saw, split, and loaded a cord of firewood into David’s old, battered, red dump truck.
I bartered my lodging for student ministry in his cabin (year-round brook for running water) by helping him in the woods as I learned horse logging. After a cold sponge bath in the brook, we drove in his truck to the nearby Rowe Conference Center in the Berkshires to schmooze with Michael Harrington and Harvey Cox at a weekend program on “Religion and Socialism.” The center accepted our offer to barter for the program with cordwood. The year was 1981.
